mesh_pivot.deviation_note: The brief's path names an 'L01' folder holding an 'L02'-named mesh; that folder does not exist on disk (confirmed by direct load_asset failure and directory listing). The real, on-disk folder for the L02 wall module is 'Kit_Bldg_CHA_L2_A' (matching the L1 kit's own naming pattern 'Kit_Bldg_CHA_L1_A'). Substituted per the coordinator's explicit ruling to pick a genuine wall module from a standard level (L2 or later) that actually exists.

read_mechanism.correction_to_task4_plan: Task 4's plan text assumes a RULE asset (BP_ShapeGrammarRule_C instance) exposes a property literally named 'grammar', writable via set_editor_property("grammar", ...). THIS IS WRONG. The asset's only top-level property is "rule" (case-insensitively also "Rule"), which returns an STC_Rule struct. That struct does NOT expose its fields via get_editor_property() on any dir()-listed name (dir() lists only generic struct methods), and its to_dict() returns an empty {}. The working read (and, by the same struct-serialization mechanism, the expected write) path is export_text()/import_text() using UE's canonical '(FieldName_GUID=value,...)' text format. The grammar field's real mangled name is 'grammar_10_4003928D40C6099DCA57829F48235D57' (identical GUID suffix across all 5 assets tested, since it's a class-level struct layout, not per-instance). Task 4 MUST be corrected to read/write via rule.export_text()/rule.import_text() (or an equivalent set_editor_properties() call keyed by the mangled name), not via get_editor_property("grammar")/set_editor_property("grammar", ...).

step4_verdict.headline: BDF<->RULE token mapping HOLDS: all 4 pairs match exactly. No contradiction found.

whitelist_nodes.headline: The style-code whitelist (CHA, CHB, ..., and where TL would be added) is a graph-level user parameter named 'BuildingsStyles' (String, default "") on /CitySamplePCG/PCG/Primitives/Buildings/Assign_CitySampleBuildings's user_parameters InstancedPropertyBag. It is NOT overridden anywhere in the two whitelist graphs named in the brief, nor at the top-level PCG_3_3_1_Buildings level graph -- every consumer relies on the empty-string default, which per its pin tooltip means 'randomly use all available building styles'.

PCG_3_3_1_Buildings.note: No node/settings property on this graph carries the literal whitelist string as a value (confirmed by both a targeted scan and a full member-dump scan). This graph's own user_parameters bag has NO BuildingsStyles entry at all (it only carries Debug/MinHeight*/MaxHeight*/Partitioned/ComplexBuildingShapes/CollisionGeometry) -- so BuildingsStyles is never surfaced for a level author to set here. It contains 3 PCGSubgraphSettings nodes (Subgraph_3, Subgraph_40, Subgraph_41) whose subgraph_instance.graph resolves to Assign_CitySampleBuildings; all 3 have subgraph_override == None, i.e. none of them override BuildingsStyles.

Assign_BldgStyles_per_MinWallWidth.note: No node/settings property on this graph carries the literal whitelist string as a value either (same two scan methods). This graph's own user_parameters bag is empty (no properties at all). It contains 10 PCGSubgraphSettings nodes (Subgraph_2, Assign_20/15/14/12/11/10/9/8/6) whose subgraph_instance.graph resolves to Assign_CitySampleBuildings; all 10 have subgraph_override == None.

hits.read_mechanism: graph.get_editor_property("user_parameters") -> InstancedPropertyBag; to_dict() returns {} (unhelpful, same pattern as STC_Rule); export_text() returns the real values, e.g. '(Value=/Engine/Transient.PropertyBag_...(...,BuildingsStyles="",...))'.
hits.note: This is the TRUE, unique edit target for adding style code TL to the whitelist: append TL (and update the tooltip's enumerated list/glossary, which lives as separate FProperty metadata -- see tooltip_metadata_not_reachable_via_api below) here, or set a subgraph_override on a specific instantiating node for a scoped change.

Assign_CitySampleBuildings_CoreProcess_c.note: This subgraph is the CoreProcessGraph referenced by Assign_CitySampleBuildings's user_parameters (see sibling_params above). It contains 56 nodes; 2 of them READ (not write) a live PCG point-data attribute named 'BuildingsStyles' (materialized from the graph user-parameter of the same name): FilterDataByAttribute_4 filters on attribute '@Data.BuildingsStyles', and DataAttributesToTags_1 maps attribute 'BuildingsStyles' to a tag. The node that WRITES/materializes the attribute from the user-parameter was not conclusively located within Task 1's time-box; these two are consumers, not the definition site. The user-parameter default itself (recorded above) remains the authoritative whitelist edit target regardless.

tooltip_metadata_not_reachable_via_api.summary: The full enumerated style-code list (CHA, CHB, CHC, ..., SFJ) and its per-code glossary (e.g. 'CHA=Chicago early 1900s office building...') exist as FProperty/pin TOOLTIP metadata on the BuildingsStyles parameter, confirmed present in Assign_BldgStyles_per_MinWallWidth.uasset's raw bytes via a byte-level scan from outside the editor (Python file read + regex, ~45 'CHA' occurrences found; no 'strings' utility was available in this environment).
tooltip_metadata_not_reachable_via_api.why_it_matters: This tooltip text is documentation metadata, NOT a live property value, and is therefore NOT reachable through get_editor_property()-based Python scans -- confirmed by an exhaustive BFS across the full 48-graph closure of both whitelist graphs named in the brief (zero string hits despite the scan mechanism being independently verified correct), plus a direct input_pins/output_pins + pin-label scan (also zero hits). Any later task that needs to update the human-readable glossary (e.g. adding 'TL=<description>' text) will need a different mechanism than get_editor_property()/set_editor_property() -- this was not resolved within Task 1's scope and should be flagged to whichever task handles documentation/tooltip text.
verbatim_tooltip_fragments: The BuildingsStyles string parameter expects a comma-separated list where entries can be one of the following: CHA, CHB, CHC, CHD, CHE, CHF, CHG, CHH, CHI, CHJ, NYAA, NYAB, NYAC, NYAD, NYAE, NYAF, NYG, NYGA, NYH, QBA, QBAA, SFA, SFB, SFC, SFD, SFE, SFJ. If the string is not set, the primitive will randomly use all available buildings styles.
BuildingsStyles=Definitions..CHA=Chicago early 1900s office building built with medium-sized white concrete blocks and hosting stores on the ground floor...CHB=Chicago 1920s office skyscraper...
